column1: # Experimental (procedural talk): templates. The spanish is a general sentence, the english has slots that the
# plugin fills in game ({thing} from pools.tsv, {day} {here} {vessel} {alt_km} from the flight, {other} and
# {self} in intercom scenes). Versions split by | are picked per play. Every version of a line must fit every
# version of the lines around it. So one clip gives many subtitles, and it is still real loñapsE. New keys: tp_

column12: english
Who took my {thing}? | Has anyone seen my {thing}? | My {thing} is gone. Again. | Okay. Who moved my {thing}? | {other}, did you take my {thing}?

column11: Yo no. Mira detrás de eso.
column12: {not_me} Look behind the {spot}. | {not_me} Try the {spot}. | Check behind the {spot}, {other}. | Last time it was under the {spot}.
Oh. Found it. Next to my {thing:2}. | Found it. It was with my {thing:2}. | Oh. There it is. | Got it. Sorry, {other}.
What is that smell? Is that {food}? | Does anyone else smell {food}? | Something smells like {food} in here. | {other}, did you heat up the {food} again?
Better not ask, {other}. | You don't want to know. | Let's just say it was {food:2}. | Don't ask. Breathe through your mouth.

column11: ¿A quién se le ocurrió este nombre?
column12: Who named this thing {vessel}? | {vessel}. Who picked that name? | Why is this ship called {vessel}? | I still can't believe we fly the {vessel}.
That was your idea, {other}. | You picked it, {other}. | You voted for it. Twice. | It was that or {silly_name}.
Well, it was a great idea. | Fine. It's a good name. | Okay. Good name. | Fair enough.
Last night I dreamt about {creature}. | I had that dream again. With {creature}. | I dreamt about {creature}. It knew my name. | Don't laugh, but I dreamt about {creature}.
Again? That's the third time, {other}. | Again? You need more sleep, {other}. | Third time this week. | Was I in it? | Again? Stop eating {food} before bed.
How long have we been out here? | What day is it? | {other}, how many days has it been? | I've lost count of the days.
Day {day}. Too many. | Day {day}, I think. | No idea. Day {day}? | Day {day}. I counted on the wall.
I thought it was fewer. | Feels like more. | That can't be right. | Huh. Only {day}?

column11: Algo se ha soltado otra vez.
column12: The {part} came loose again. | {other}, the {part} is loose again. | Is the {part} supposed to wobble like that? | Something rattles. I think it's the {part}.
Tape it, like the {part:2}. | Tape. Same as always. | Just use tape, {other}. | Tape it. Don't tell Control.

column11: Control, se nos ha acabado la comida buena.
column12: Control, we are out of {food}. | Control, someone ate all the {food}. | Control, the {food} is gone. Send more. | Control, food report: zero {food} left.

column11: Os queda mucha de la otra.
column12: You still have plenty of {food:2}. | Eat the {food:2}. | There's a full crate of {food:2}. | Try the {food:2}. It builds character.

column11: Control, la vista desde aquí es increíble.
column12: Control, the view of {here} from up here is amazing. | Control, you should see {here} from here. | Control, {here} looks so small from up here. | Control, I could look at {here} all day.
Glad to hear it, {vessel}. Back to work. | Nice. Now back to work, {vessel}. | Enjoy it. Then get back to work. | Take a picture. Then work.
Control, how high are we? | Control, what's our altitude? | Control, how far up are we now? | Control, are we in space yet?
About {alt_km} kilometers. Enjoy the view. | {alt_km} kilometers. Don't look down. | High enough. About {alt_km} km. | {alt_km} km, {vessel}. Enjoy it.
